Reentries.title: Reentries

toolbar.flyToCorridorTooltip: When enabled, clicking a TIP row flies the camera to the predicted reentry corridor on the globe instead of following the object.
toolbar.corridorNote: The TIP location is not an impact point. The object could come down anywhere along its ground track during the window.
toolbar.showAllColumnsTooltip: The menu is too narrow for every column, so some are hidden. Turn this on to show them all and scroll the table sideways.

help.overview: The Reentries menu tracks objects falling out of orbit. It has two tabs: official reentry predictions from US Space Command, and a live analysis of the lowest objects in the catalog.
help.imgAlt: The Reentries menu showing the TIP Messages table
help.imgCaption: TIP reentry predictions. Clicking a row jumps the simulation to the predicted decay time.
help.tabs:
• TIP Messages: Tracking and Impact Prediction messages published by US Space Command, with the predicted decay time, location, uncertainty window (plus or minus minutes around the decay time), reentry angle, RCS, and mass. Clicking a row selects the object and jumps the simulation time to the predicted decay epoch. With Fly to corridor on, the object is still selected, but the camera flies to the predicted decay location on the globe instead of following the object.
  • Reentry Analysis: roughly 200 cataloged objects sorted by lowest perigee. Rows are color coded: red means the object has reentered (perigee below 120 km, or its elements can no longer be propagated), yellow means perigee below 160 km (high risk). Clicking a row selects the object.
help.corridor:
A TIP message gives one predicted decay time and location, plus a window of plus or minus minutes. The object moves at about 7 to 8 km per second, so every minute of uncertainty is roughly 450 km along its ground track. The object could come down anywhere along that track during the window; the TIP location is the middle of that stretch, not an impact point.

The corridor still matters because it is the only ground the object can overfly during the window. Regions far from the track are not at risk from this object in this window, and the regions under it are the ones that need warnings, airspace or maritime notices, or observers ready to watch for and report a fireball. Each new TIP message shortens the window, and the corridor narrows to fewer and fewer passes.
help.howToUse:
1. Open the menu from the drawer or press Shift+R.
  2. Click Fetch Data to load the latest TIP messages (requires an internet connection). After the first load the button becomes Refresh.
  3. Click any prediction to fly to that object at its predicted decay time.
  4. Switch to the Reentry Analysis tab to browse what is decaying next. It loads the first time you open it.
help.tip1: A "Reentered" entry in the Mean Alt column means the object can no longer be propagated. It has most likely already come down.
help.tip2: TIP predictions carry real uncertainty: the Window column is plus or minus that many minutes around the decay time, so the full window is twice as long and can span continents of ground track.
help.tip3: Clicking a TIP row silently changes the simulation clock to the decay epoch. Use the time controls to come back to the present.

Reentries.dataSource: Tracking and Impact Prediction (TIP) messages provided by the US Space Command (USSPACECOM).
